Run a command in a sandbox, with an identity of its own

## Usage

```console
coder run [flags] [--template <template> | <workspace>] [-- command...]
```

## Description

```console
Run a command as a workload. The workload gets its own identity, sponsored by you. It can do nothing in Coder unless you give it scopes, and it never receives your credentials. The command's output is streamed and its exit code returned.

With --template, the workload gets a workspace of its own: a new workspace is made from the template for this one command and deleted when the command is over. With a sandbox template that takes about a second. Without --template, the workload runs in a sandbox that the daemon of an existing workspace creates.
  - Run a command in a workspace of its own and see who it is:

     $ coder run --template sandbox -- coder identity

  - Keep the workspace afterwards, to look around in it:

     $ coder run --template sandbox --keep --name fix-1 -- make test

  - List your workloads in every workspace, with what became of each:

     $ coder run --all

  - Run a command in a sandbox inside one of your workspaces:

     $ coder run my-workspace -- coder identity

  - Let a workload list your workspaces:

     $ coder run my-workspace --scope workspace:read --scope template:read -- coder list

  - Work in a sandbox with a terminal:

     $ coder run -it my-workspace -- sh

  - List the running workloads of a workspace:

     $ coder run --list my-workspace

  - List all of them, with what became of each:

     $ coder run --all my-workspace

  - Remove a workload:

     $ coder run --remove workload-1a2b3c4d my-workspace
```

## Options

### --name

| Property | Value               |
|----------|---------------------|
| Type     | <code>string</code> |

A name for the workload.

### --scope

| Property | Value                     |
|----------|---------------------------|
| Type     | <code>string-array</code> |

A permission the workload may use on your behalf, as an API token scope such as workspace:read. Repeat it for several. Without any, the workload can do nothing in Coder.

### --image

| Property | Value               |
|----------|---------------------|
| Type     | <code>string</code> |

The image for the workload's sandbox. The workspace's template sets the default and decides which others are allowed.

### --network

| Property | Value               |
|----------|---------------------|
| Type     | <code>string</code> |

What the sandbox can reach: "none" or "outbound". The workspace's template sets the default. With "none" the workload can still reach Coder, and nothing else.

### --mount

| Property | Value                     |
|----------|---------------------------|
| Type     | <code>string-array</code> |

A directory of the workspace to show in the sandbox, at the same path. It is read-only unless followed by ":rw". Repeat it for several. The workspace's template decides which directories may be shared; without this flag the workload sees nothing of the workspace.

### --template

| Property | Value               |
|----------|---------------------|
| Type     | <code>string</code> |

Give the workload a workspace of its own, made from this template and deleted when the command is over. Use a sandbox template, whose workspaces are claimed from a warm pool, for a start in about a second.

### --keep

| Property | Value             |
|----------|-------------------|
| Type     | <code>bool</code> |

With --template, keep the workspace when the command is over. It stays as it is, and can be looked at and removed like any workspace.

### --agent

| Property | Value               |
|----------|---------------------|
| Type     | <code>string</code> |

The workspace daemon to run the workload in, by name. Only needed when the workspace has several.

### -i, --interactive

| Property | Value             |
|----------|-------------------|
| Type     | <code>bool</code> |

Keep the command's input open. Use it with --tty, as -it.

### -t, --tty

| Property | Value             |
|----------|-------------------|
| Type     | <code>bool</code> |

Give the command a terminal and attach to it. Use it with --interactive, as -it.

### -d, --detach

| Property | Value             |
|----------|-------------------|
| Type     | <code>bool</code> |

Start the workload and print its name instead of following its output.

### -l, --list

| Property | Value             |
|----------|-------------------|
| Type     | <code>bool</code> |

List the workspace's running workloads instead of running one.

### -a, --all

| Property | Value             |
|----------|-------------------|
| Type     | <code>bool</code> |

List the workspace's workloads, including the most recent ones that are over.

### --logs

| Property | Value               |
|----------|---------------------|
| Type     | <code>string</code> |

Print the output of a workload, by name or identity, instead of running one. A running workload is followed until it ends. For one that is over, the end of its output was kept.

### --remove

| Property | Value               |
|----------|---------------------|
| Type     | <code>string</code> |

Remove the named workload instead of running one.
